title: Knockout Ladder: Heuristic-evals and Version Stability Matrix
content:
Purpose and short summary:

This note captures the results of a focused 'knockout ladder' style evaluation run that compares three candidate serving artifacts (v3.2-fp16, v3.3-int8, v3.4-quant) plus the current production baseline (v3.1-prod). The aim was to profile stability across diverse prompt perturbations, measure head-to-head win/loss on our core prompt sets, and generate rollout criteria (canary/rollback) for the next deployment.

Key differences from prior bakeoffs:
- We intentionally focused on heuristic perturbations (typos, instruction rephrasings, context truncations) rather than only held-out QA pairs.
- Introduced micro-cohort telemetry that simulates spotty connectivity and low-token budgets to stress caching/batch logic.
- Added a compact semantic-fidelity metric derived from pairwise human judgments (see scoring appendix).

Experiment design:
- Candidates: v3.1-prod (baseline), v3.2-fp16, v3.3-int8, v3.4-quant
- Prompt sets: core-support-1000 (customer support intents), creative-500 (long-form generation), sys-instr-200 (instruction-following), edge-parsing-150 (structured parsing failure modes)
- Perturbations applied: whitespace noise, random-case, punctuation-deletion, leading-context-truncation (50/100 tokens), max-tokens cap at 32 (low-budget)
- Micro-cohorts: stable-net, flaky-net (simulated 250ms jitter/10% drop), low-budget (token cap)
- Metrics: head-to-head win_rate (human pairwise), semantic_fidelity (0-1), hallucination_rate (%), avg_latency_ms (99p), token_cost_per_1k, response_variance (std over repeated runs), edgecase_failure_rate
- Human annotation: 600 pairwise comparisons sampled across prompts and cohorts (balanced across variants)

Top-level findings (short):
- v3.4-quant yields the lowest token_cost (approx -38% vs prod) and best throughput but shows a modest increase in hallucination_rate on edge-parsing prompts (+1.8 percentage points).
- v3.3-int8 offers a compromise: ~-22% cost, small latency wins, and generally parity in semantic_fidelity with baseline across support and creative sets.
- v3.2-fp16 tracked closest to production on quality metrics but provided only marginal cost improvement (-8%).
- Win/loss ladder: v3.3-int8 narrowly beats v3.2-fp16 in head-to-head human wins; v3.4-quant beats both on average score but had higher variability (response_variance).

Leaderboards (aggregate ranks; higher is better for fidelity/wins, lower better for cost/latency):

Aggregate Leaderboard (normalized ranks 1=best)
---------------------------------------------------------------
Model         | WinRate  | SemFid | Halluc% | 99pLat(ms) | Cost/1k
---------------------------------------------------------------
v3.3-int8     | 0.47     | 0.78   | 3.9     | 130        | $2.1
v3.4-quant    | 0.51     | 0.76   | 5.7     | 210        | $1.3
v3.2-fp16     | 0.44     | 0.79   | 3.1     | 150        | $3.0
v3.1-prod     | 0.38     | 0.76   | 4.2     | 170        | $2.1
---------------------------------------------------------------
Notes: winrate is pairwise human win fraction aggregated; SemFid is normalized human-derived score. Cost/1k is estimated end-to-end token cost including routing overhead.

Win/Loss pairwise matrix (wins over rows vs columns; sample sizes vary 100-200 per pair)
----------------------------------------------------------------
          | prod | v3.2 | v3.3 | v3.4
----------------------------------------------------------------
prod      |  -   | 38/100 | 24/120 | 22/110
v3.2-fp16 | 62/100 |  -    | 28/110 | 30/105
v3.3-int8 | 76/120 | 72/110 |  -    | 44/115
v3.4-quant| 88/110 | 75/105 | 71/115 |  -
----------------------------------------------------------------
Interpretation: v3.4 wins many pairwise comparisons, especially on creative prompts, but human comments reveal more frequent confident-sounding but incorrect statements on structured edge cases. v3.3 is a robust middle ground.

Stability matrix (by cohort):
- Stable-net: all candidates comparable; v3.4 slightly faster under batching.
- Flaky-net: v3.4 shows increased variance in final tokens leading to higher edgecase_failure_rate (2.7% vs baseline 1.1%).
- Low-budget: v3.3-int8 performs best when token cap at 32; v3.4 truncates more aggressively and sometimes drops critical instruction tokens (observed 18% of low-budget parses).

Regression flags observed:
- Edge parsing hallucination spike: v3.4 edge-parsing hallucination_rate = 9.4% vs baseline 7.6% (stat sig at p<0.05 after Bonferroni correction).
- Instruction-drop under low-budget: v3.4 misses required instruction in 18/100 synthetic low-budget tests vs 4/100 for v3.3.
- Latency tail: v3.4 99p latency increases notably under flaky-net (210ms vs 170ms prod), linked to kernel fallback on certain attention dims.

Human annotation highlights (representative comments):
- "v3.4 sounds more decisive but invented a date that wasn't present" (creative prompt 332)
- "v3.3 kept to the instructions and was shorter but correct" (support prompt 88)
- "v3.2's enumerated list matched reference; small language differences only" (sys-instr 21)

Rollback / Canary triggers (proposed):
- Canary rollout (10% production traffic) for v3.3-int8:
  - Auto-abort if moving 24h average hallucination_rate > 1.5x prod baseline OR if semantic_fidelity drops > 0.04 absolute.
  - Auto-abort if 99p latency > 2x prod 24h average.
- Hold v3.4-quant to internal dedicated clusters until edge-parsing failure sources are mitigated. Do not canary on support-critical routes.

Suggested path forward and actionable items:
1) Promote v3.3-int8 to 10% canary across non-critical routes (support-sandbox + creative) for 7 days with real-time gating. Owner: Daniel Rivera.
2) Spin up targeted debug harness for v3.4 focusing on attention kernel fallbacks and tokenization edgecases. Owner: Lena Cho.
3) Add 1k prompt perturbation tests into CI that replicate low-budget truncation cases; threshold fail if instruction-drop rate > 5%. Owner: Marco Alvarez.
4) Re-run a smaller knockout focusing solely on edge-parsing with enlarged annotation (n=1500) before considering v3.4 wider rollout. Owner: Asha Menon.

Appendix: scoring and statistical notes:
- Semantic_fidelity is computed from pairwise comparisons where annotators choose A/B/both/neither; normalized to [0,1] by (wins - losses)/total with smoothing. Inter-annotator Kappa = 0.61 on sampled subset.
- All p-values reported are from two-tailed bootstrap resampling unless noted. For multiple comparisons we applied Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.05 except where Bonferroni was explicitly used.
- Cost estimates include model inference token counts, average batch utilization, and routing overhead approximated from prod traces during the same 7-day window.

Questions for review (items to resolve in PRD):
- Acceptable trade-off curve for hallucination vs cost for support routes (CS preference likely: lower hallucination even at +10-20% cost).
- Are we willing to accept v3.4 as a dedicated-only offering to start (cheaper for high-throughput internal jobs) while protecting public support endpoints?

End of note.
